passages.text: Some time later God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am,” he answered.
passages.sermon:
God is the Creator and ruler of all things.
Abraham is a faithful servant of God.
After these events, God tested Abraham.
God spoke to Abraham.
God called out, “Abraham!”
Abraham answered, “Here I am.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְהָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים נִסָּ֖ה אֶת־ אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: “Take your son,” God said, “your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Abraham.
God said, “Take your son Isaac.
Isaac is your only son.
You love Isaac.
Go to the land of Moriah.
Offer Isaac there as a burnt offering.
Offer him on one of the mountains.
I will show you which mountain.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר קַח־ נָ֠א אֶת־ בִּנְךָ֙ אֶת־ יְחִֽידְךָ֤ אֲשֶׁר־ אָהַ֙בְתָּ֙ אֶת־ יִצְחָ֔ק וְלֶךְ־ לְךָ֔ אֶל־ אֶ֖רֶץ הַמֹּרִיָּ֑ה וְהַעֲלֵ֤הוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה עַ֚ל אַחַ֣ד הֶֽהָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So Abraham got up early the next morning, saddled his donkey, and took along two of his servants and his son Isaac. He split the wood for a burnt offering and set out for the place God had designated.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man chosen by God.
God tested Abraham.
God told Abraham to offer his son Isaac as a burnt offering.
The next morning, Abraham got up early.
He saddled his donkey.
He took two of his servants with him.
He took his son Isaac with him.
He split wood for the burnt offering.
Abraham set out for the place God had told him about.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם אַבְרָהָ֜ם בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַֽיַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ אֶת־ חֲמֹר֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֤י נְעָרָיו֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֖ת יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֑וֹ וַיְבַקַּע֙ עֲצֵ֣י עֹלָ֔ה וַיָּ֣קָם וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ אֶל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ אָֽמַר־ ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man who obeyed God.
On the third day, Abraham traveled with his son Isaac and two servants.
Abraham looked up.
He saw the place God had told him about.
The place was far away.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֧ם אֶת־ עֵינָ֛יו וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת־ הַמָּק֖וֹם מֵרָחֹֽק׃

passages.text: “Stay here with the donkey,” Abraham told his servants. “The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will return to you.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a faithful servant of God.
He spoke to his two servants.
He said, “Stay here with the donkey.”
He said, “The boy and I will go over there.”
He said, “We will worship God.”
He said, “We will return to you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶל־ נְעָרָ֗יו שְׁבוּ־ לָכֶ֥ם פֹּה֙ עִֽם־ הַחֲמ֔וֹר וַאֲנִ֣י וְהַנַּ֔עַר נֵלְכָ֖ה עַד־ כֹּ֑ה וְנִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה וְנָשׁ֥וּבָה אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac. He himself carried the fire and the sacrificial knife, and the two of them walked on together.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was Isaac’s father.
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering.
He placed the wood on Isaac, his son.
Abraham carried the fire in his hand.
He also carried the sacrificial knife in his hand.
Abraham and Isaac walked on together.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־ עֲצֵ֣י הָעֹלָ֗ה וַיָּ֙שֶׂם֙ עַל־ יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ אֶת־ הָאֵ֖שׁ וְאֶת־ הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו׃

passages.text: Then Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” “Here I am, my son,” he replied. “The fire and the wood are here,” said Isaac, “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Abraham’s son.
Abraham was Isaac’s father.
Isaac spoke to Abraham.
Isaac said, “My father!”
Abraham answered, “Here I am, my son.”
Isaac said, “We have the fire.”
Isaac said, “We have the wood.”
Isaac asked, “Where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִצְחָ֜ק אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֤ם אָבִיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֔י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֶּ֣נִּֽי בְנִ֑י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה הָאֵשׁ֙ וְהָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאַיֵּ֥ה הַשֶּׂ֖ה לְעֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: Abraham answered, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” And the two walked on together.
passages.sermon: Abraham spoke to Isaac, his son.\r\nAbraham said, “God will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.”\r\nAbraham and Isaac walked on together.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֱלֹהִ֞ים יִרְאֶה־ לּ֥וֹ הַשֶּׂ֛ה לְעֹלָ֖ה בְּנִ֑י וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם יַחְדָּֽו׃

passages.text: When they arrived at the place God had designated, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was Isaac’s father.
God told Abraham to go to a certain place.
Abraham and Isaac arrived at the place God chose.
Abraham built an altar there.
Abraham arranged the wood on the altar.
Abraham tied up his son Isaac.
Abraham placed Isaac on the altar.
Abraham put Isaac on top of the wood.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ אֶֽל־ הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר־ ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ וַיִּ֨בֶן שָׁ֤ם אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת־ הָעֵצִ֑ים וַֽיַּעֲקֹד֙ אֶת־ יִצְחָ֣ק בְּנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֹתוֹ֙ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ מִמַּ֖עַל לָעֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man who obeyed God.
He reached out his hand.
He took the knife.
He prepared to kill his son Isaac.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶת־ יָד֔וֹ וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־ הַֽמַּאֲכֶ֑לֶת לִשְׁחֹ֖ט אֶת־ בְּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven, “Abraham, Abraham!” “Here I am,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke from heaven.
The angel called to Abraham.
The angel said, “Abraham, Abraham!”
Abraham answered.
Abraham said, “Here I am.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֵלָ֜יו מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ מִן־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַבְרָהָ֣ם׀ אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him,” said the angel, “for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me.”
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke to Abraham from heaven.
The angel said, “Do not lay a hand on the boy.
Do not do anything to him.
Now I know that you fear God.
You have not withheld your only son from me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־ תִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָֽדְךָ֙ אֶל־ הַנַּ֔עַר וְאַל־ תַּ֥עַשׂ ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָּה כִּ֣י׀ עַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־ יְרֵ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ אַ֔תָּה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֛כְתָּ אֶת־ בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת־ יְחִידְךָ֖ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. So he went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a faithful servant of God.
Abraham looked up.
He saw a ram behind him.
The ram was caught in a thicket by its horns.
Abraham went to the ram.
He took the ram.
He offered the ram as a burnt offering.
He offered the ram instead of his son.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־ עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ וְהִנֵּה־ אַ֔יִל אַחַ֕ר נֶאֱחַ֥ז בַּסְּבַ֖ךְ בְּקַרְנָ֑יו וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אַבְרָהָם֙ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־ הָאַ֔יִל וַיַּעֲלֵ֥הוּ לְעֹלָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת בְּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. So to this day it is said, “On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man who obeyed God.
Abraham named that place “The LORD Will Provide.”
People still say this today.
They say, “On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַבְרָהָ֛ם שֵֽׁם־ הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא יְהוָ֣ה׀ יִרְאֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יֵאָמֵ֣ר הַיּ֔וֹם בְּהַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרָאֶֽה׃

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time, saying, “By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that because you have done this and have not withheld your only son, I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time.
The angel spoke to Abraham.
The LORD said, “I have sworn by Myself.”
The LORD made this promise.
The LORD said, “You have done this thing.”
Abraham did not withhold his only son.
Because of this, the LORD said, “I will surely bless you.”
The LORD said, “I will greatly multiply your descendants.”
Your descendants will be as many as the stars in the sky.
Your descendants will be as many as the sand on the seashore.
Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֛א מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֑ם שֵׁנִ֖ית מִן־ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֗י יַ֚עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֙יתָ֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א חָשַׂ֖כְתָּ אֶת־ בִּנְךָ֥ אֶת־ יְחִידֶֽךָ׃ כִּֽי־ בָרֵ֣ךְ אֲבָרֶכְךָ֗ וְהַרְבָּ֨ה אַרְבֶּ֤ה אֶֽת־ זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְכַח֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ שְׂפַ֣ת הַיָּ֑ם וְיִרַ֣שׁ זַרְעֲךָ֔ אֵ֖ת שַׁ֥עַר אֹיְבָֽיו׃

passages.text: And through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Abraham.
God said Abraham obeyed His voice.
God promised Abraham a blessing.
God said Abraham’s offspring would bring blessing.
God said all nations on earth would be blessed through Abraham’s offspring.
passages.original: וְהִתְבָּרֲכ֣וּ בְזַרְעֲךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ עֵ֕קֶב אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ בְּקֹלִֽי׃

passages.text: Abraham went back to his servants, and they got up and set out together for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was the man God chose to bless.
Abraham returned to his servants.
The servants stood up.
Abraham and his servants traveled together.
They went to Beersheba.
Abraham lived in Beersheba.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שָׁב אַבְרָהָם֙ אֶל־ נְעָרָ֔יו וַיָּקֻ֛מוּ וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו אֶל־ בְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אַבְרָהָ֖ם בִּבְאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃פ

passages.text: Some time later, Abraham was told, “Milcah has also borne sons to your brother Nahor: Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel (the father of Aram), Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was the son of Terah.
Abraham had a brother named Nahor.
Some time after these events, someone brought news to Abraham.
The person said, “Milcah has also given birth to sons for your brother Nahor.”
Milcah was Nahor’s wife.
Milcah bore several sons to Nahor.
The first son was Uz.
The second son was Buz, Uz’s brother.
The third son was Kemuel.
Kemuel became the father of Aram.
The other sons were Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְאַבְרָהָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הִ֠נֵּה יָלְדָ֨ה מִלְכָּ֥ה גַם־ הִ֛וא בָּנִ֖ים לְנָח֥וֹר אָחִֽיךָ׃ אֶת־ ע֥וּץ בְּכֹר֖וֹ וְאֶת־ בּ֣וּז אָחִ֑יו וְאֶת־ קְמוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִ֥י אֲרָֽם׃ וְאֶת־ כֶּ֣שֶׂד וְאֶת־ חֲז֔וֹ וְאֶת־ פִּלְדָּ֖שׁ וְאֶת־ יִדְלָ֑ף וְאֵ֖ת בְּתוּאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight sons to Abraham’s brother Nahor.
passages.sermon:
Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.
Milcah gave birth to eight sons.
Milcah was the wife of Nahor.
Nahor was Abraham’s brother.
passages.original: וּבְתוּאֵ֖ל יָלַ֣ד אֶת־ רִבְקָ֑ה שְׁמֹנָ֥ה אֵ֙לֶּה֙ יָלְדָ֣ה מִלְכָּ֔ה לְנָח֖וֹר אֲחִ֥י אַבְרָהָֽם׃

passages.text: Moreover, Nahor’s concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
passages.sermon:
Nahor had a concubine.
Her name was Reumah.
Reumah gave birth to Tebah.
Reumah gave birth to Gaham.
Reumah gave birth to Tahash.
Reumah gave birth to Maacah.
passages.original: וּפִֽילַגְשׁ֖וֹ וּשְׁמָ֣הּ רְאוּמָ֑ה וַתֵּ֤לֶד גַּם־ הִוא֙ אֶת־ טֶ֣בַח וְאֶת־ גַּ֔חַם וְאֶת־ תַּ֖חַשׁ וְאֶֽת־ מַעֲכָֽה׃ס
